outline.title: Abstract
outline.description: A concise summary of the survey's scope, covering the evolution of LLM security from 2023 to 2026. It highlights the transition from simple prompt exploits to sophisticated architectural vulnerabilities, poisoning of reasoning processes, and the security implications of autonomous agentic systems. The abstract concludes with the necessity of holistic defense frameworks and standardized evaluation metrics.

outline.title: Introduction
outline.description: This section motivates the critical need for LLM security research given the rapid deployment of generative AI in sensitive domains. It outlines the scope of the survey, covering the period from 2023 to 2026, and identifies the core contribution: a comprehensive synthesis of training-time and inference-time threats. It introduces the four primary pillars of the survey: adversarial attacks, poisoning, hallucinations, and prompt injection, while emphasizing the shift toward 'Reasoning LLMs' (RLLMs) and autonomous agents.

outline.title: Background and Preliminaries
outline.description: Provides the foundational knowledge required to understand LLM vulnerabilities. It covers LLM architectural basics (Transformer, MoE), the alignment pipeline (SFT, RLHF, DPO), and the fundamental threat model. Key definitions such as Attack Success Rate (ASR), Jailbreaking, and Indirect Prompt Injection (IPI) are established. This section also introduces the Chain-of-Thought (CoT) mechanism, which becomes a central target for attacks in later sections.

outline.title: Data and Model Poisoning: Training-Time Vulnerabilities
outline.description: Analyzes how attackers manipulate the LLM supply chain and alignment process. It discusses the fragility of RLHF and DPO against label-flipping [Baumgartner_2024_RLHF, Kusaka_2025_LLM] and the injection of backdoors in specialized domains like code generation [Yan_2024_LLM, Hossen_2024_Double]. A major focus is the 2025 shift toward 'behavioral' and 'reasoning' poisoning, where the internal logic of Large Reasoning Models (LRMs) is hijacked to induce deceptive reasoning [Zhu_2025_Think, Shen_2025_Decepchain]. It also covers multilingual backdoor transferability [He_2024_LLMs].

outline.title: Adversarial Attacks: Exploiting Model Mechanics
outline.description: Explores the evolution of adversarial exploits from early prompt-based triggers to deep architectural vulnerabilities. It details white-box analysis tools used to measure backdoor manifestations in neuron activations [Cheng_2024_Unit, Hussain_2024_Measuring]. The section covers 'context-shifting' strategies that bypass guardrails via expert programming frames [Noever_2024_AI] and the weaponization of LLM agents for autonomous CVE exploitation [Fa...]. It highlights the transition from single-turn exploits to multi-turn conversational history manipulation [Hao_2024_Exploring].

outline.title: Prompt Injection and Jailbreaking: Interaction-Based Threats
outline.description: Focuses on the manipulation of model instructions during inference. It reviews structural vulnerabilities like 'FlipAttack' [Liu_2024_Flipattack] and automated black-box generation frameworks like 'AutoDan' [Liu_2024_Autodan]. A significant portion is dedicated to Indirect Prompt Injection (IPI) in multi-modal and agentic environments, such as web navigation and code editors [Shi_2025_LLM, Wang_2025_Webinject]. The section also addresses new vulnerabilities in Reasoning LLMs (RLLMs) like DeepSeek-R1 related to their internal CoT processes [Cui_2025_LLM, Cui_2025_LLMs].

outline.title: Hallucinations and Factual Integrity
outline.description: Examines the security implications of non-factual generations. It covers visual hallucinations in Multimodal LLMs (MLLMs) caused by 'language priors' [Wang_2024_Mllm, Xing_2024_Mitigating] and the use of Natural Language Inference (NLI) for factual consistency checking [Jing_2024_Scale, Zhang_2024_Comparative]. The section highlights the 2025 trend of using specialized small-scale models (e.g., Paladin) for hallucination detection [Ivry_2025_Paladin, Yaron_2025_GPT] and explores domain-specific challenges in climate science and healthcare [Thulke_2025_Listen, Agarwal_2].

outline.title: Cross-Cutting Defenses and Mitigation Strategies
outline.description: Provides a holistic overview of defense mechanisms. It covers training-time interventions like robust RLHF and DPO, and inference-time guardrails such as perplexity filters and prompt sanitization. The section explores internal activation monitoring to detect adversarial triggers [Cheng_2024_Unit] and the use of specialized 'judge' models to filter hallucinations and injections. It emphasizes the need for multi-layered defense-in-depth strategies that address both structural and behavioral vulnerabilities.

outline.title: Testing Methodologies and Evaluation
outline.description: A critical synthesis of how LLM security is measured. This section catalogs benchmarks and datasets mentioned across the literature, such as AdvBench for jailbreaking and RMCBench [Chen_2024_Rmcbench] for model robustness. It evaluates metrics like Attack Success Rate (ASR), perplexity-based detection, and NLI-based consistency scores. The section also discusses the role of automated red-teaming frameworks and the challenges of evaluating autonomous agents and reasoning models where traditional static benchmarks may fail to capture dynamic vulnerabilities.

outline.title: Discussion and Open Challenges
outline.description: Synthesizes the current state of the field, identifying critical gaps such as the lack of robust defenses for autonomous agents and the 'cat-and-mouse' game between automated jailbreak generation and alignment. It discusses the limitations of current benchmarks in the era of Reasoning LLMs and the ethical implications of red-teaming research. Future directions include the development of verifiable safety properties and more efficient, domain-specialized grounding techniques.

outline.title: Conclusion
outline.description: Summarizes the key findings of the survey, reiterating the shift from surface-level prompt exploits to deep-seated reasoning and architectural vulnerabilities. It provides practical recommendations for researchers and practitioners, emphasizing that LLM security must be an integral part of the entire model lifecycle, from data curation to deployment in autonomous systems.
